title: Rotate Image (in-place 90°)
description: Rotate an n×n matrix 90° clockwise in place by transposing then reversing each row.

notes: Transpose + row-reverse equals 90° clockwise. Reverse columns instead for counter-clockwise.
Inner loop starts at `j = i + 1` so you don't swap each pair twice (and back to original).
In-place — no auxiliary matrix. Mutating the input is the whole point of the problem.

questions.q: Which two operations compose into a 90° clockwise rotation?
questions.explain: Transposing reflects across the main diagonal; reversing each row then flips horizontally, equivalent to a 90° clockwise rotation.

questions.q: Why does the transpose loop start `j` at `i + 1`?
options: To avoid swapping each pair twice (which restores the original)
O(n log n) time, O(1) space

questions.q: To rotate 90° counter-clockwise with the same trick, what changes?
options: Transpose, then reverse each column (or reverse rows first, then transpose)

blanks.hint: skip the diagonal and already-swapped pairs
Array method that mutates in place

L3.prompt: Write `rotate(matrix)` that rotates an n×n matrix 90° clockwise in place. Log `JSON.stringify(matrix)` after rotating [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]].
hints: Transpose first: swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for j > i.
Then reverse each row in place.
